items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: And so Sylvester Scott played for all of them

ctx.x: Well, Sylvester Scott would go upstairs. He would be the piano player, and he would have Lillian Randolph, you'd have Sue Hoye, Paul Howard's wife. You'd have Betty Treadwell. Well, these three people. There may have been somebody else, but I can't think right offhand. But these three people were featured, you know, entertainers. Now, they had already worked

downstairs, but they would also work this breakfast club, you know. And so Sylvester Scott played for all of them and they used to make money like it was going out of style. Now, that's another thing where the kitty came in, because nobody was making any, you know, big salary. $2.00 a night, you know, that was the extent of it. I don't think anybody was making much more than that. And they -- but they made tips, they made very good tips.
And the Alabam and breakfast club were next door to the dining room, right?
